source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
EdgeCore Ashburn AS02 is a 114 MW IT capacity campus in Sterling, Virginia, the third largest of the 25 Virginia data centers that publish a megawatt figure.

That ranking matters more than the raw number. Virginia maps 330 data centers but only 25 disclose capacity, and those 25 total 1,603 MW. One facility therefore accounts for 7.1 percent of all published state capacity. The disclosed subset is not a sample of the whole, it is the visible tip, and it is concentrated enough that a single campus moves the state total.

The 114 MW is the part that connects to AI. At 400 watts per rack for training workloads, the reading puts this at roughly 285 racks, or about 2,280 high-end accelerators at 8 GPUs per rack. That is a scale at which power delivery, not floor space, sets the ceiling. The 685,000 square feet and LEED certification describe the building, but the megawatt figure describes what the building can actually run.

What the data does not cover is the constraint that decides whether this capacity grows. Virginia's grid limits on further expansion are not published here. The site sits 3.5 miles from Dulles in the Ashburn core, inside existing power and network backbone, but nothing in this record says how much more load that backbone can absorb.
